program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is truncated and too vague to encode the full requested transformation. More importantly, its completion rule treats s1’s broad “overall reads as pencil drawing” judgment as sufficient, even though the trace describes substantial residual color and photographic detail; that endpoint-only rule collapses partial progress into yes and conflicts with the reference partial. Refine the typed criteria to distinguish visible stylistic progress from complete fulfillment, using the requested transformation and image evidence rather than accepting s1’s pass as conclusive. Ensure the partial-progress check can be evaluated when completion is uncertain, and make its dependency/activation routing explicit so a skipped s2 is not mistaken for negative evidence or silently bypassed when needed. The skipped s2 is a conditional-skip transport/coverage fact, not evidence against the edit; the concern is the semantic sufficiency threshold and routing, not that the image shows no progress. Preserve uncertainty when evidence cannot resolve completion, and do not hard-code the reference label as ground truth.
s1: The binding is truncated and the current criterion makes a broad “reads as pencil drawing” pass sufficient, so visible but incomplete stylization can be mislabeled as full fulfillment. Clarify the typed decision rule to assess both requested style transformation and retained photographic/color rendering: distinguish clear progress from completion, without treating residual color or detail alone as decisive. The trace reports pencil-like shading and contours alongside substantial photographic detail, so use that mixed evidence to avoid collapsing progress into yes; preserve unknown when the image cannot resolve completion. Make any partial-progress check’s activation and dependencies explicit so it is evaluated when needed. Treat a skipped check as routing/coverage information, not negative visual evidence, and do not encode the reference label as ground truth.
